as_told.title: Woman's death witnessed at LAX, time slows and sound returns

plain: In the 1980s, while a woman was dying after being struck as a pedestrian at Los Angeles airport, all the noise around went silent except her breathing, says Brent Friedman, a Hollywood writer who was there with her. He tells Michels that time seemed to slow, that in a place as loud as LAX "I heard nothing except her breathing," and that the moment she died, "all of the noise came back."
